Konami working on a new, likely Kojima-free Metal Gear - Destructoid

~Everyone enjoy The Phantom Pain, it will be the last.

~But what of Silent Hill(s). Could Hideo Kojima take what he started and turn it into a new separate IP?

I am okay with Konami continuing Metal Gear without Kojima. He never intended to end the series when he left, it was always meant to go on. The only problem is that he obviously won't be able to hand pick his successor. As a MASSIVE MGS fan for my entire life I don't really trust Konami to do it right. I wish Kojima had been able to leave on good terms and personally choose the person to take up the Metal Gear mantle.

But who am I kidding, I will still buy and play anything they put the Metal Gear name on. Good luck Kojima, I know you will still make amazing games. I can't wait to see what you do next.

I'm a mega fan too and I'll love the series forever. I even loved Portable Ops which Kojima was only a Producer for. I'm also thinking after everyone plays The Phantom Pain then we can decide if the series should continue. It may very well be the quintessential ending to an astounding series? Although I can see Konami attempting to woo the fans with remakes of Metal Gear 1 & 2.

I would actually be excited for Konami to remake Metal Gears 1 and 2. I haven't played them as I couldn't get over how dated they felt when I tried. Twin Snakes was a lot of fun because it was still based on Kojima's original vision. Remakes of Metal Gear 1 and 2 are about the only things I would want Konami to do.

This is true, lest we forget, Twin Snakes was a Silicon Knights Project and it was also published by Nintendo so of course it had to be almost Perfection if it were to be released. (LOL.. Denis Dyack) Anyways, I must admit, I played Twin Snakes before I played the original Metal Gear Solid because I never had a Playstation in the 90's. We tried it on my good friends PSX. But it was way too hard for us. I think we were like 13-14 if I recall. That being said if handled appropriately (which we know is not always Konami's strong suit) I would love remakes of Metal Gear 1 & 2.

~Oh and one more thing, we were talking about Grey Fox over on that other post. Remember what Hideo Kojima just said two weeks ago about how Snake won't say much in The Phantom Pain? In other words he's a "Projection of the Player" I feel like that is a major clue right there that it's definitely not the real Big Boss. I've not gotten all the way through that video yet (if they mentioned it) but that just popped in my head. :)

I have to admit I'm actually going to be disappointed if we don't get to hear Snake spouting philosophy about life, war, love, or any of the other things I'm used to hearing him ramble about. I have a feeling Snake "not saying much" means something very different to Mr. Kojima than it does to the rest of us. More likely we just won't have any 15 minute soliloquies from him in this one XD

Oh me too, I've had friends say they "don't like all that talking in their games" where I'm like are you kidding me, that's one of my favorite parts is hearing all the codec conversations or the cassette tape recordings in Peace Walker. They literally talked about everything, from wild life to film to Japanese History. Oh and speaking of Peace Walker, that Gray Fox Video also reminded me that Null was Frank Jaeger aka Gray Fox in Portable Ops! I completely forgot about that. And for not paying him much attention I totally do now after watching that entire hour and twelve minute video. My goodness. And if you think about it. All of the Metal Gear Heroine have had their own game. Raiden, Solid Snake, Big Boss, technically all that's left is Frank. I don't know why he's always flown under my radar? I mean people love him, but I guess I've always been more focused on the Villains and now, who and what makes Big Boss evil? Here's another thing, do you think if we are indeed playing as Frank Jaeger, somewhere in the middle or end of the game we have a showdown with the real Big Boss (voiced by David Hayter)? He keeps suggesting and alluding that he's involved. And of course he's been trolling since the announcement two weeks ago, doing interviews and tweeting. I do hope so, I mean his voice is imprinted in my brain forever as Snake. I'm sure a young Solid Snake is going to make an appearance similar to how Liquid appears in the Trailer as Eli. But there's no way Hayter can pull off the voice of a 12 year old. lol :)

One more thing, I wonder if there is anything to this "Deprivation Tank Theory" And that Ground Zeros was all a dream or Training Simulation in Frank's mind and he actually entered the Body of Big Boss in this dream, since Big Boss is his best and only friend, he wanted to become him (?) (which would explain the voice change in Ground Zeros.)
